content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices correct downward.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment drives short-term price momentum.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment remains stable or shows consistent bullish signals.", "Model bias is more pronounced in low-volume periods, indicating reduced market liquidity affects forecast reliability.", "Forecast lags often occur when sentiment shifts abruptly, suggesting delayed reaction to sentiment changes.", "High sentiment volatility leads to forecast divergence, indicating model struggles with rapid sentiment swings.", "Model underestimates sharp price drops when sentiment turns negative, indicating failure to capture downside risk.", "Forecast accuracy improves when recent history shows strong upward momentum, suggesting momentum persistence enhances model performance."]}
